---
name: make-reel
description: Run the reel pipeline for one source link (an arXiv paper, or an engineering article for a system-design reel): direct, check the script on a cold viewer, produce, check, then publish according to policy. Use when the user supplies a link and wants a video made.
---
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-agents.mjs from .claude/agents. Do not edit. -->

Argument: an arXiv URL, a benchmark URL, or an engineering article URL. Optionally a format (`paper` or `system-design`).

Formats live in `paper-reels/formats/`. An arXiv link is `paper`. An engineering blog post or design write-up is `system-design`. If you cannot tell, ask the human before step 1.

1. **Direct.** Spawn `reel-director` with the URL and the format. It saves the source and writes `treatment.md`. Read the chosen hook; if it is a topic label rather than a claim or question, or it uses a term a newcomer does not know, send it back once (SendMessage to the same director).
2. **Cold viewer, on the treatment.** Copy the `Script` block of the treatment (the spoken lines, `l01: ...`) and spawn `cold-viewer` with only those lines in the prompt: no file paths, no topic summary, no URL. Compare its say-back with the treatment's one idea. On FAIL, or when the say-back misses the idea, send the director (SendMessage, same agent) the whole list sorted: points flagged in more than one round first, cheap real defects next, points to ignore last (a hero named in the hook and explained later is by design). Check again. Stop after three rounds and report what is still unclear.
3. **Script phase.** Spawn `reel-producer` with the URL, the treatment path and "script phase". It registers the item and writes `storyboard.json`, `facts.json` and `evidence.json`, with `ste.mjs` at 0 hard findings, and stops.
4. **Cold viewer, on the storyboard.** Extract the spoken lines (`node -e` over `storyboard.json`, `id: text` per line). If they are word for word the script that passed step 2, skip this step. Otherwise run step 2 on them, with fixes going to the same producer (SendMessage). At most three rounds.
5. **Build phase.** Spawn a fresh `reel-producer` with the episode folder and "build phase". A new spawn, not the script-phase agent: the build needs the storyboard, not the source text and the history of the script rounds. It renders, registers and runs `validate.mjs` until PASS.
6. **Check, in parallel.** Spawn `retention-critic` and `reel-validator` at the same time for the item id. Both are read-only. Merge their findings into one list (validator failures first, then the critic's top fixes) and send it to the build-phase producer (SendMessage). It reports which line ids and scenes changed. Then run both checkers again: give the validator the changed line ids so it re-checks only those claims. Stop after three rounds and report what is still failing. Both reviews are tied to the video's hash, so the last round must cover the final render.
7. **Publish**, by policy:
   - `settings.autopublish` is off (default): show the human the verdict, scores, decoded-frame sheet, thumbnail, post text and the last cold-viewer say-back, and ask for approval. On an explicit yes in chat, record it: `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs approve <id> --platforms youtube,instagram --quote "<the human's exact words>"`. Never run `approve` without the human's yes for these files. If the files change after the yes, show them again and ask again: the record goes stale. Then post it yourself:
     1. `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs publish <id> --platforms youtube,instagram --dry-run`. If it prints REFUSE, stop and report each line. Do not look for a way around a refusal.
     2. `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs publish <id> --platforms youtube,instagram`. Do not use `--force` unless the human asked for a repost and the old posts are marked DELETED.
     3. `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs show <id>`: report each platform's URL and status and the `notion vault:` line. If the vault line says FAILED, do not retry; tell the human to run `reels notion-sync`. If a platform failed, report the error and stop; do not retry in a loop.
   - `settings.autopublish` is on: run `node paper-reels/bin/reels.mjs autopublish <id>`; it posts only if every gate holds and otherwise parks the item as `needs_review` and notifies.
8. **Thread (paper only).** Once the Instagram reel of a `paper` episode is live, invoke the `make-thread` skill with the paper link and the Instagram reel URL, without being asked. It asks the human for a yes before posting (unless `settings.autopublish` is on). If the reel is not live yet, say that the thread will follow after posting. A failed thread never undoes the reel. For a `system-design` episode, skip this step and say so.
9. Report the URLs (reel and thread), or what is waiting on the human.

Never skip validation or the cold-viewer check. Never let the producer judge its own output. Never run two renders of one episode at once. A `system-design` run is long (voice for 40 to 60 lines, a render of about 6 minutes): run every step in the foreground.
